payload.label: Workflow recipes: step-by-step playbooks any person's AI can follow, one file each in recipes/
Start a run of a recipe: leave its steps as a job for my AI
payload.job: When a recipe of mine is started, by a wake I switched on or by a call, put its steps and its input in my own records as one job waiting for my AI, once per firing
payload.description: Every recipe row runs as this tool (the recipes' row source names it in invoke_with), with the recipe's id in input.row. It reads that recipe from the person's own list of workflows and the rows of its steps, or else from the public recipes folder (the person's own row wins when both hold the id; their rows may be typed record:workflow-recipe or workflow-recipe, arrivals/recipe-row-types.json), and, when a record wake names an arrival source, starts only from the changed rows that source's filter keeps, each a seed in the run's input, writing nothing when none is kept (arrivals/arrival-sources.json); it writes one record of kind ai-job, id ai-job:<recipe id>:<request key>, holding status waiting, the recipe id and label, its steps, the input it was started with and the wake cause that started it. It does no step itself, schedules nothing and keeps nothing else. The AI that next connects to the person's records lists ai-job records with status waiting, does the oldest, and writes status done with its result. A firing or a call that comes again with the same request key finds its job and writes nothing.

row.description: The recipe's id (workflow:...). The engine sets it to the recipe row being run.

start_at.description: The step the run starts at, when a wake names one

arrival_source.description: A row of the person's own list arrival-sources, when a record wake starts the run: only the changed rows its filter keeps start it, each made a seed in the run's input (seeds); when it keeps none, nothing is written (arrivals/arrival-sources.json)

job.description: The id of the ai-job record, null when nothing arrived

record_model._what: The record kinds, indexes and links this tool keeps (moved unchanged from trillion-rust's one record model: src/record_model_policy/record-model.json, src/record_indexes/record-indexes.json, product/lists.json field_kinds and product/record-sharing.json links).

kinds._read_by: Every share surface writes one record shared:<request key> when the person leaves File in on You figure it out (trillion ios/Shared/ShareRecord.swift, extension/src/share-record.mjs); the Workshop recipe turn-something-shared-into-what-you-can-use wakes on this kind and files it. items are {kind: link, url} | {kind: selection, text} | {kind, name, file: <file identity>}.

record_model._what_moved: Moved here from tools/keep-a-record-library-valid, where they were held unchanged after the engine's one record model left it (old trillion src/record-model.json and src/record-indexes.json): the kinds this tool's job keeps, each as old trillion declared it.

rules_and_runs._what: The record kinds the engine's rules and workflow runs (trillion-rust src/rule_bindings/rules_and_runs.rs) read and write for this account, moved from trillion-rust src/rule_bindings/rules_and_runs/settings.json, there from old trillion src/automations.mjs and src/workflows.mjs: `rule` is the kind of a rule row (its id is the kind, a colon and the rule's id), `outcome` the kind the trigger rules' own writes are kept as when they name none, `run` a workflow run's row, `recipe` the row holding a workflow's definition, `send` the row a rule's send to a tool is kept as for the wake runner, and `own` every kind these rules and runs write, never handed to the rules as a change. With this tool not installed, no rule runs.

payload.label: Choose which of my workflows fire for these parts of a seed
payload.job: Say which of all my workflows, and the Workshop's I have installed, fire for each part of something that arrived, from the conditions each workflow carries on its own row
payload.description: Every workflow is a candidate branch of the one tree. Takes parts: the parts of one seed, each an object of its typed fields (for example kinds, subjects, people, niches, own_words; the fields are whatever the conditions read). Reads every workflow row the person has (their list of workflows under each type arrivals/recipe-row-types.json lists) and every recipe this Workshop installs; when both hold an id the person's row wins, and when it holds no conditions the installed recipe's are used. Each workflow's conditions are its fires_when (branches/fires-when.json): a list of { label, condition: { fields, tree }, made_by, state }, the same fields and tree tool:filter-rows-by-rules takes, evaluated by the same formulas engine over the parts. Answers chosen (one row per workflow, part and condition that kept it), unfinished (conditions with a rule the engine cannot evaluate or no rule at all, which choose nothing), unconditioned (workflows with no condition On, by id and label, to be judged by their words), unmatched_parts and the counts. Nothing is written; no workflow, branch or tag is named in the tool.

parts.description: The seed's parts, each an object of the typed fields the conditions read

operators.description: Comparisons and combinators as rows of data, as tool:filter-rows-by-rules takes them; left out for the built-in ones

parts.words: A finding: most small teams never write their plan down.

payload.label: Start the agents of one step of a recipe run: one waiting job per lane
payload.job: When a step of a recipe run says it has several agents, start that many jobs for it in my own records, each with its own lane, so each lane is done by its own AI
payload.description: Reads the run (the ai-job tool:start-a-recipe-run wrote) and its step, whose own row says how many agents run it (agents, one whole number, 1 when left out) and may name the lanes (lanes). A step with one agent starts nothing. Otherwise it writes one waiting ai-job per lane, id <run id>:<step id>:<lane id>, holding the step, the run's input and cause, the lane and a note telling that AI to do only its lane. The jobs are written in batches that fit the door, the step's first lane last, so a start that comes again finds the first lane's job and changes none, even one an AI already finished. The step's lane-jobs check refuses an answer unless every lane names its own such job and that job ran.

run.description: The id of the run's ai-job (ai-job:<recipe id>:<request key>)

step.description: The id of the step in that run whose agents to start

jobs.description: The ids of the lane jobs, one per agent; empty when the step has one agent

checks.says: Every lane comes from its own job that ran

payload.label: Start one step of a recipe run and get its work, with its lane jobs when it has several agents
payload.job: Begin a step of my recipe run: get the step with what to do, and when it says it has several agents have each agent's own job started in my own records, in the same call
payload.description: Reads the run (the ai-job tool:start-a-recipe-run wrote) and its step. A step with one agent is handed back as it is. A step whose agents is above 1 has its lane jobs started by this same call (tool:start-a-steps-agents does the writing, in door-sized batches, none twice), so the run's AI has no separate start to leave out; the lane jobs are handed back with the step. Each lane's job is then done by its own AI. tool:submit-a-recipe-step refuses an answer for lanes whose jobs never ran.

run.description: The id of the run's ai-job (ai-job:<recipe id>:<request key>)

step.description: The id of the step to begin
The step as the run holds it: id, title, do, submit, checks, agents, lanes

as.description: The AI id this lane takes and finishes its job under

take.description: The exact command that takes the lane's job as that id

finish.description: The exact command that finishes it as that id

lane_jobs.description: Each lane, the id of the ai-job that runs it and the commands to take and finish it under its own AI id; empty when the step has one agent

checks.says: Every lane comes from its own job that ran

payload.label: Hand in the answer to one step of a recipe run, judged by the step's checks on what the records hold
payload.job: Hand in my answer to a step of my recipe run, and have it kept only when the step's checks pass, judged on what my own records say ran
payload.description: Reads the run, the step and the answers kept for the steps before it, and judges the step's checks. The ran-job catalog the lane-jobs check looks in is built here from each lane's own ai-job (<run>:<step>:<lane>): a lane's job ran when its status is done, and its taker is who finished it. The caller gives only run, step and answer; an input that carries a catalog or anything else is refused. A failing check refuses the answer and keeps nothing; a check that cannot be judged here is listed as unchecked, never as passed. A passing answer is kept as the ai-job <run>#answer:<step>; a submit that comes again finds it and changes nothing.

run.description: The id of the run's ai-job

step.description: The id of the step answered

answer.description: The step's answer, in the shape the step's submit says

unchecked.description: Checks that could not be judged here, with the reason

checks.says: Every lane comes from its own job that ran
Every lane comes from its own job that ran
Every lane comes from its own job that ran

payload.label: Run a read-only checklist gate on my files (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Before I am shown anything I made, list the required checks that apply to it and identify which answers are open, stale or failed, without changing my files
payload.description: Reads the person's checklist (stages, checks and routes), schema and piece from one folder they grant. It runs the existing checklist gate read-only: every required check that applies to the piece is listed with its current answer state, file identity and criterion pins. It accepts `gate`, `scope`, `audit` without `--hold`, read-only `checklist`, and `library-pending` for the next bounded source-assessment batch in the schema's current work context. It does not create a lock file, first-gate record or pin cache, and it cannot answer checks, run write-producing sweeps or hold files. The same generic checklist consumer still refuses empty or unknown scopes, reports stale answers and requires exact BLAKE3 file and definition pins. A separate write-grant tool handles commands that change the library. Nothing about a person's checklist or piece is known by this tool; the schema owns those details.

library.description: The folder the schema's files are relative to, put where {library} is in the command.

schema.description: The schema file on the person's computer (see the README for its keys), put where {schema} is in the command.

command.description: A read-only command: gate <piece> --stage ID[,ID] [--option ITEM]... [--at DELIVERY_STAGE]; scope <piece> [--lane NAME]; audit <piece> [--file PATH]...; checklist [--check|--problems]; or library-pending --limit 8 [--source-id ID]. Never include --hold or --write. Put the command after the schema in the command.

output_schema.description: { result, exit_code } from the existing gate consumer. For gate, result contains all_passed, the routed checks, stale or failed answers, and items not evaluated; scope lists item ids; audit lists offenders; checklist reports its generated comparison or problems. exit_code is 0 when the selected read passes, 1 when a gate is open or failed, and 2 for unreadable inputs. The private native run omits temporary answer command paths.

provenance.source: A pre-delivery gate over a person's own checklist where every answer is bound to the identity of the files it judged and every measuring tool's answer to the reviewed version of that tool

payload.label: Turn my written checklist into the checklist file the gate reads, and check that file (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Keep one written checklist of mine as the only source, generate the checklist document from it, tell me when the file on disk no longer matches my text, and find the mistakes a hand edit or a typo would make
payload.description: Reads a person's checklist text (one section per stage, one table row per check, notes that annotate a check, an optional file of rules whose wording is read from there and never copied) through the `checklist_source` part of the schema the person gives, which holds the regular expressions and constant fields that say how their text is laid out. `checklist` prints the document the text generates, `--check` says in words which checks differ from the file on disk, `--write` writes the file, and `--problems` checks the file on disk for repeated ids, a required flag that is not true or false, a route no reader can evaluate, a per-item check with no rule, an advisory stage that is not a delivery stage, a phase that names no check and counts that do not add up. It refuses a rule that has no row and a note that names no check. It knows no row kind, id shape or route tag.

library.description: The folder the schema's files are relative to, put where {library} is in the command.

schema.description: The schema file on the person's computer (its checklist_source part is described in the README), put where {schema} is in the command.

mode.description: One of: --check, --write, --problems, or leave it out to print the generated document. Put it where {mode} is in the command.

output_schema.description: --check and --problems print { all_passed, difference? | problems }; --write prints { written, checks, must }; with no mode the generated document. The exit status is 0 when everything passed, 1 when the file differs or has problems and 2 when the text or schema could not be read.

invoke.say: This runs on the person's own computer, from the root of the Workshop checkout. After the person edits their written checklist, run it with `--check`; if it says the file differs, run `--write`, then `--problems`, and tell the person what the text now generates and any problem found. Never edit the generated file by hand: the text is the source.

provenance.source: A checklist document generated from the person's own text by declared patterns, so there is one source and a check that the generated file has not drifted

payload.label: Record a checklist answer or run its checked steps (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Record a checklist answer or run a declared checker or gate, with the required folder change grant
payload.description: Uses the same checklist consumer as the read-only gate, but only after the person grants this tool permission to change one folder. It records the person's answer, imports a checker report under the reviewed checker pins, runs the schema's sweeps or gates, holds files only when requested, writes the checklist generated from the person's text, or records and removes source assessments in the existing applications DATA through `library-assess` and `library-remove`. Assessments require current source and work-context pins and preserve other contexts. The existing consumer still checks criteria definitions, BLAKE3 file pins, checker pins, scopes and stale rows; this tool adds no alternate answer or bypass.

library.description: The library folder inside the folder you grant for this run.

schema.description: The schema file inside the folder you grant for this run.

command.description: A write command: answer <piece> --check ID [--option ITEM] --answer pass|fail|n/a --evidence TEXT --by NAME; answers-from-report <piece> --json REPORT [--option ITEM]; sweep <piece> --previews FOLDER...; run-gates <piece> --lane-dir FOLDER; run-files <piece> --file PATH...; audit <piece> --hold; checklist --write; library-assess --json FILE; or library-remove --json FILE. The command is parsed as arguments, never shell text.

output_schema.description: { result, exit_code } from the existing checklist consumer, or { error, exit_code } when the command cannot run. An open or failed check remains failed; an answer is kept only under its own name and current file and criterion pins.

provenance.source: tools/workflows/do-work/checklist_gate.py: answer and checker operations share the same criterion, file and checker pins as the read-only gate

# Sample checklist

**Delivery stages:** final = a loaf put on the shelf.

## S1. Bake
| S1.1 | Oven is preheated | all | Read the dial | habit | yes |
| S1.2 | Tray is clean | all | Look at it | habit | no |

## Notes

payload.label: Measure exact page citations across planned questions and answer engines
payload.job: Compare every planned page × question × answer engine cell against recorded answer observations, keeping exact page citations, unavailable answers and unasked cells distinct
payload.description: Builds the complete page × question × engine matrix from a plan and supplied observations. A citation counts only when its parsed HTTP(S) URL exactly matches the page URL, its supplied checked canonical URL, or an explicitly supplied verified redirect URL; a path prefix is never enough. Query strings remain significant and fragments are ignored. Original answers and citation links are preserved. Missing/not-run and unavailable cells stay unknown; only an observed answer with an explicit citations array can be cited or not cited. This tool measures supplied observations and does not query engines, establish who observed them, or prove why an engine cited a page.

questions.description: Questions this exact page answers; otherwise shared questions must be supplied.

canonical_url.description: Canonical address observed from the page; include only when checked.

verified_redirects.description: Redirect addresses actually observed while reaching this page.

questions.description: Shared questions planned for every page that does not provide its own questions.

provenance.source: tools/workflows/read-data/citation-coverage.mjs: complete planned matrix and exact checked page URL identities
